result: In 21 CFS patients, electrical pain thresholds were significantly lower than controls in deltoid, trapezius and quadriceps muscle (P<0.001) but normal in skin and subcutis.
reason: Measures resting pain thresholds vs controls; adds tissue specificity (deep muscle, not skin) to the hyperalgesia claim; small, no exercise or CPM testing.

result: Quadriceps biopsies in 9 CFS patients (vs 4 controls) showed sarcomere alterations, fatty degeneration, abnormal mitochondria, reduced mitochondrial enzyme activities and a 150-3000-fold increase in the 4977 bp mtDNA common deletion.
reason: Reports marked structural and mitochondrial abnormalities, the opposite of the finding's mostly normal/nonspecific histology; very small sample.

result: None of 34 CFS patients' muscle biopsies contained enteroviral RNA by RT-PCR; muscle RNA/DNA ratio and mitochondrial enzyme activities were generally reduced, consistent with inactivity.
reason: Tests muscle, not stomach VP1/RNA; fits the old-biopsy finding's point that Bowles-type muscle EV RNA was not reproduced and changes are nonspecific (same as companion link).

result: None of 34 CFS patients' muscle biopsies contained enteroviral RNA by RT-PCR; muscle RNA/DNA ratio and mitochondrial enzyme activities were generally reduced with no specific enzyme defect, consistent with reduced habitual activity.
reason: Null EV RNA and only nonspecific biochemical changes support, rather than contradict, the finding that older biopsy abnormalities were nonspecific and Bowles EV RNA not reproduced.

result: Serum IGF-I and IGFBP-3 did not differ between 15 CFS, 15 CFS-FM, 27 FM patients and 15 healthy controls, nor did the proportion outside the reference range.
reason: Same measure (serum IGF-I); null result replicates the intact GH/IGF side of the finding; small groups.

result: In 76 CFS patients vs 69 controls, CD11b on CD8 cells was decreased, previously reported CD38 and HLA-DR increases were not confirmed, and no marker correlated with fatigue severity.
reason: Measures surface activation markers by basic immunophenotyping, not exhaustion transcription/chromatin programmes; no atlas finding covers CD38/HLA-DR activation markers; cytokine part handled by companion link.

result: Circulating cytokines did not differ between 76 CFS patients and 69 matched controls, and endotoxin-stimulated ex vivo TNF-alpha and IL-1 beta production was significantly lower in CFS.
reason: Tests circulating cytokines and finds no difference (and lower stimulated TNF), against the meta-analytic small TNF elevation.

result: No enterovirus was found in 34 CFS patients by faecal isolation (including acid treatment to dissociate immune complexes), serum-CSF antibody testing (7 pairs) or muscle PCR (29 biopsies).
reason: No stomach biopsy or VP1 staining; muscle PCR null supports the old-biopsy finding that Bowles muscle EV RNA was not reproduced.

result: HMPAO SPECT showed generalised reduced brain perfusion and brainstem hypoperfusion in ME/CFS (0.72 vs 0.80 in pilot, p<0.0001; 0.71 vs 0.77 in depressed patients, p<0.0001) in 67 patients vs 40 controls plus depressed and epilepsy comparison groups.
reason: Same measure (resting SPECT perfusion), independent cohort, lower perfusion; orthostatic status not recorded.

result: Brainstem hypoperfusion on HMPAO SPECT was found in all ME/CFS patients and was lower than in depressed patients (0.71 vs 0.77, p<0.0001).
reason: Brainstem imaging difference by another modality and team, distinguishing ME/CFS from depression; supports the repeated brainstem finding.
